subject: Discovery recap + next steps (NovaAnalytics) - reprioritize or shelve?
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Lina Wu <lina@novaanalytics.com>, Chris Thomas <chris.thomas@novaanalytics.com>
Cc: Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-01T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Discovery recap + next steps (NovaAnalytics)

Hi Lina / Chris —

Thanks again for the conversation today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Highlights from our call:
- Primary use case: real-time anomaly detection in customer event streams (90% of queries under 1s).
- Data: ~200M events/day, prefixed keys and semantic embeddings would be ideal; sensitive PII in columns A/B (needs masking).
- Compliance: Nova needs SOC2 + EU data residency for future expansion; initial pilot can run in us-west.
- Success metric: reduce manual triage time by 60% and <1.5s 95th percentile latency for inference.

Proposed next steps (what I can do this week):
1) Share a 2-week PoC plan + pricing estimate (attached: redwood-trial-poc-plan.pdf, pricing-estimate-v1.xlsx).
2) Provide a sandbox trial tenant and a small sample model to validate latencies with your sample dataset — Maya will own the security checklist.
3) 45-minute technical workshop with your infra/ML eng team to validate embedding strategy and KV-caching approach (I propose Wed 5/5 at 10am PT).

Ask from your side: please share a non-sensitive sample (5-20k events) or a synthetic export and confirm whether the pilot uses AWS us-west or a VPC subnet (for the security checklist).

If this plan looks good I’ll send a calendar invite and loop Maya for the SOC2/arch notes. If timing has shifted, just reply with where this sits on your priority list.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this forward.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: redwood-trial-poc-plan.pdf (PoC timeline and acceptance criteria), pricing-estimate-v1.xlsx (pilot pricing bands)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Lina Wu <lina@novaanalytics.com>
Cc: Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-02T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap + next steps (NovaAnalytics) — quick check-in

Hi Lina —

Just nudging this up the inbox in case it got buried. Quick reminder of the two asks that unblock the trial: one small sample export (or synthetic equivalent) and a preferred pilot region (us-west or VPC). I drafted the PoC scope and attached it on Friday.

If now is not the right time, no problem — can you give me a sense of timing? A quick option: if you want to keep this alive, pick one of these windows for the tech workshop and I’ll lock it in:
- Wed 2027-05-05 10:00–10:45 PT
- Thu 2027-05-06 15:00–15:45 PT

If neither works reply with a proposed time or simply say ‘not prioritizing’ and I’ll update our pipeline accordingly.

Thanks,
— Marcus

> On May 1, 2027, at 15:12, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com> wrote:
> > (see original recap and attachments)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Lina Wu <lina@novaanalytics.com>
Cc: Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-03T09:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap + next steps (NovaAnalytics) — closing the loop?

Hi Lina —

I haven’t heard back and wanted to close the loop. I know priorities shift — if Nova is no longer moving forward with this pilot in the near term, let me know and I’ll shelve the file on my side (won’t follow up further).

If you are still interested but timing is delayed, reply with an ETA and I’ll set a reminder and keep the draft PoC available. If you’d like one quick call to reassess priority, here’s a short scheduling link: https://calendly.com/redwood/marcus-15

Either way, happy to keep the door open. Just want to avoid pinging too often.

Best,
— Marcus
